prisoner.name: Mary Lane
prisoner.description: Mary Lane organized voter registration in Greenwood and served as a SNCC project director. She spent 48 days imprisoned at Parchman in 1963 and later represented the Mississippi Freedom Democratic Party at the 1964 Democratic National Convention.

cases.charges: Imprisonment following Greenwood civil-rights organizing; individual statutory charge unverified
cases.sentence: Forty-eight days actually spent at Parchman in 1963. Exact custody endpoints and imposed sentence remain unverified.

case_research.custody_evidence: Her individual SNCC/Duke biography explicitly reports48days of imprisonment, not only an arrest or proposed term.

entries.custody_evidence: Her individual SNCC/Duke biography explicitly reports48days of imprisonment, not only an arrest or proposed term.
entries.status_research: Historical custody verified. Existing profiles, cases and photos are preserved. No unsupported vital dates, coordinates, current incarceration, institutional relation or personal support website inferred. No June25 arrest inferred from Cotton’s account. The delegate group photograph is not cropped because her precise position is unverified. Unrelated artist,writer and obituary namesakes excluded.

prisoner.name: Douglas MacArthur Cotton
prisoner.description: Douglas MacArthur Cotton was a Mississippi Freedom Rider and SNCC voter-registration organizer. His imprisonment included a Freedom Ride case and a later Greenwood prosecution that sent him to the county farm and Parchman. His sworn account also documents a separate 1964 detention in Natchez.

cases.charges: Freedom Ride arrest after attempting to buy a ticket at the segregated bus station
cases.sentence: Thirty-nine days on death row are documented. Arrest and imprisonment began in 1961; exact endpoints and sentence unverified. Placement on death row does not imply a death sentence.

cases.charges: Disturbing the peace during Greenwood voter registration
cases.sentence: Convicted June 25, 1963; four months hard labor and $200 fine. His affidavit records 55 days at Parchman after county-farm confinement. Released on bond in August 1963; exact day unverified.

cases.charges: Initially held for auto-theft investigation; subsequently charged with vagrancy
cases.sentence: Thirty hours detained with George Greene during voter-registration work in Natchez in late February 1964. Exact days and disposition unverified.

case_research.custody_evidence: The oral-history archive identifies the1961 imprisonment; SNCC/Duke documents39days actually confined.
Sworn account establishes actual sustained custody; later first-person interview places release before the1963 March on Washington.55days is the Parchman portion, not total custody.
Cotton expressly distinguishes this30-hour detention from shorter repeated stops; it exceeded one day.

prisoner.name: George Greene
prisoner.description: George Greene was a Greenwood civil-rights organizer who worked with SNCC and the NAACP youth movement. His 1963 imprisonment included the Leflore County Penal Farm and Parchman. He continued voter-registration work after release.

cases.charges: Arrest during a Greenwood demonstration; exact statutory charge unverified
cases.sentence: Six-month hard-labor sentence and $500 fine; the interview-based history reports 67 days actually served before his father obtained release. Custody included county farm and Parchman; exact endpoints unverified.

cases.charges: Initially held for auto-theft investigation; subsequently charged with speeding
cases.sentence: Thirty hours detained with MacArthur Cotton during voter-registration work in Natchez in late February 1964. Exact days and disposition unverified.

case_research.custody_evidence: Payne distinguishes Greene’s actual67days from his imposed six-month sentence; SNCC biographies corroborate the1963 Parchman episode.
The co-detainee’s sworn account names Greene and reports the shared30-hour confinement and different charges.

March1964 Ruleville incident in Congressional Record testimony lasted11–12hours and is excluded from the multi-day case list. Do not confuse with the separate February Natchez detention.
